title: Results object
aliases:
  - attributes.html
---

`model.fit()` returns a `Results` object. Its everyday attributes are direct,
named `pandas.Series` or scalar values; optimizer implementation details are
kept under `optim_result`.

## Results: everyday use

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| `params` | Estimated coefficients indexed by variable name. |
| `bse` | Standard errors indexed like `params`. |
| `tvalues` | Test statistics indexed like `params`. |
| `pvalues` | Two-sided p-values indexed like `params`. |
| `conf_int()` | Confidence intervals for the coefficients. |
| `nobs` | Number of observations used in the fit. |
| `df_resid` | Residual degrees of freedom. |
| `llf` | Maximized log-likelihood. |
| `aic`, `bic` | Information criteria. |
| `converged` | Whether optimization converged. |
| `random_effects` | Object exposing `.group` and `.time` residual effects and standard deviations. |
| `resid` | Regression residuals. |
| `fittedvalues` | Fitted dependent-variable values. |
| `summary()` | Formats a human-readable regression summary. |

```{python}
#| eval: false
results.params
results.bse
results.summary()
```

## Optimizer internals (advanced)

Advanced diagnostics are available from `results.optim_result`, including
`hessian`, `gradient_matrix`, `gradient_vector`, `dx_norm`, `its`, `msg`,
`t0`, `t1`, and `log_likelihood_object`.

The former `output` and `table` objects are implementation details and are
private as `results._output` and `results._table`.
